record.paper_title: Electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions: progress and open questions
record.original_question: How far down in photon transverse momentum and dilepton invariant mass can perturbative hard-scattering formulas for prompt photons and Drell-Yan dileptons be used in proton-proton and nucleus-nucleus collisions, especially when photons with transverse momentum of roughly 1–5 GeV or below may be non-perturbative or require large non-perturbative corrections, and when the most interesting heavy-ion photon signal lies at low transverse momentum?

evidence.quote: A crucial question regarding Equations 4 and 5 is: how low in transverse momentum can they be used?

When Equation 4 is compared with data from proton-proton collisions, it is understood that the photon p_T^γ must be at least a few GeV for the perturbative Equation 4 to be valid; photons with p_T^γ ≲ 1–5 GeV are assumed to be produced non-perturbatively, or at least have significant non-perturbative corrections, though calculations of these non-perturbative processes are generally not available.
This is a challenge, since the most interesting photon signal in heavy-ion collisions is at low p_T^γ. The analogous challenge for dileptons is the low-invariant-mass limit of Drell-Yan dileptons.
A better understanding of these low-p_T^γ/low-invariant-mass regimes in proton-proton collisions would benefit the study of electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In high-energy hadronic collisions, prompt-photon production and Drell–Yan dilepton production are commonly described by collinear-factorized perturbative QCD formulas of the form

  E_γ dσ^{γ}/d^3 p = ∑_{a,b} ∫ dx_a dx_b f_{a/A}(x_a, μ_F) f_{b/B}(x_b, μ_F) · (E_γ dσ̂^{ab→γ X}/d^3 p)(μ_R, μ_F),

  dσ^{ℓ⁺ℓ⁻}/dM² = ∑_{a,b} ∫ dx_a dx_b f_{a/A}(x_a, μ_F) f_{b/B}(x_b, μ_F) · (dσ̂^{ab→ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ X}/dM²)(μ_R, μ_F),

where f_{a/A} are parton distribution functions of hadrons or nuclei A, B, dσ̂ are partonic cross sections computed in fixed-order perturbation theory, μ_R, μ_F are renormalization and factorization scales, p_T^γ denotes the transverse momentum of the produced photon, and M denotes the invariant mass of the produced lepton pair.

Determine, with quantitative theoretical control, the lower boundary in p_T^γ (for prompt photons) and the lower boundary in M (for Drell–Yan dileptons) below which these perturbative hard-scattering formulas cease to provide a reliable description in (i) proton–proton collisions and (ii) nucleus–nucleus collisions. In particular, characterize and compute the non-perturbative corrections that become important in the regime p_T^γ ≲ 1–5 GeV and at low dilepton invariant mass, and establish a controlled framework that extends the validity of the perturbative description (or systematically supplements it with non-perturbative contributions) into the soft regime relevant to electromagnetic probes of heavy-ion collisions.
artifact.status_search_result: No general theoretical solution is established for the validity boundary of collinear-factorized prompt-photon and Drell–Yan formulas at low p_T and low invariant mass; quantitative non-perturbative corrections in this regime remain an active open research area, with ongoing work on small-x, TMD factorization, and resummation but no consensus closed-form answer.

status_evidence.snippet: A crucial question regarding [the perturbative formulas] is: how low in transverse momentum can they be used? ... calculations of these non-perturbative processes are generally not available.
status_evidence.claim: The low-p_T / low-mass validity boundary of perturbative prompt-photon and Drell–Yan formulas is identified as an open question.
